AbilitiesOut.description:
What the caller may do with it now (`abilities.py`): the same rules the actions
enforce.
AbilitiesOut.title: AbilitiesOut

ActivityAccount.title: ActivityAccount

ActivityAutomation.description:
The automation a notification is about (it was paused: plan M7); its agent is
the entry's `author`; `paused_reason` why it is paused now (`owner`, `failing`,
`manual`), null once it runs again.
ActivityAutomation.title: ActivityAutomation

ActivityConversation.description:
`name` is null for a direct message and a page or ticket thread; `page_id` names
a page thread's page, `ticket_number` a ticket thread's ticket (null for other
kinds; the ticket's address is `/tickets/<number>`).
ActivityConversation.title: ActivityConversation

ActivityCountOut.description: `open`: not done; `unread`: not done and not read (the badge).
ActivityCountOut.title: ActivityCountOut

ActivityOut.description:
A notification: why, where, from whom, and the first 140 characters of the
message's Markdown. `parent_id`: the thread the message is in (null: top level).
`read_at`/`done_at`: null until marked. An `assignment` points at a timeline entry:
`author` is who assigned, `snippet` is empty. A `proposal` for a new page at the top
level has no conversation and no message, but `proposal` (plan M6); a
`skill_proposal` has `skill_proposal` instead (plan M6 task 9), an `automation`
the automation (plan M7), a `signup` the waiting account (plan M9); `author` may be
an agent (`type`).
ActivityOut.title: ActivityOut

ActivityProposal.description:
The proposal a notification is about when it has no thread to point at (a new
page at the top level; its address: the space's proposals).
ActivityProposal.title: ActivityProposal

ActivitySkillProposal.description:
The skill proposal a notification is about (a skill has no thread; its address:
`/api/skill-proposals/{id}`); `space_id` none: organisation-wide.
ActivitySkillProposal.title: ActivitySkillProposal

AdminTokenOut.description:
A token in the admins' list: its metadata and whose it is (`user`: its person;
for an agent token the agent's responsible person, and `agent` the agent).
AdminTokenOut.title: AdminTokenOut

AgentCreate.description:
`connection_id`/`model`: a chat connection of the organisation and one of its
models. `responsible_user_id`: an active person (no guest) who answers for it.
Both are needed for the organisation's agents (`agent.manage`). `personal`: the
caller's own agent (`agent.create_personal`), which takes the caller's connection
and model and has the caller as responsible person (given, they must be those).
`kind: external` (plan M8 decision 11, `agent.manage`): an agent that works from
outside through `/mcp`; no connection, no model, not personal, level at most 2
(else 422 `agent.external_invalid`), a responsible person required.
AgentCreate.title: AgentCreate

AgentExternalToolOut.description:
What an external tool is (plan M8 decision 8): its server and its name there;
`usable`: approved, unchanged and on an enabled server (else a run never gets it,
whatever the entry says). `left_out`: granted and usable, but left out of every
model call by the bound on all of the agent's external tool definitions (module
review M8 2, finding G5): the tools listed first come first.
AgentExternalToolOut.title: AgentExternalToolOut

AgentOut.description:
An agent as those who manage it see it (`agent.manage`; a personal agent's
owner); `responsible_name`: the responsible person's name; `owner_user_id`: a
personal agent's owner (null: the organisation's). `kind`: `external` for an
agent that works from outside through `/mcp` (plan M8): no connection or model
(both null).
AgentOut.title: AgentOut

AgentPickOut.description: An agent to set a budget for.
AgentPickOut.title: AgentPickOut

AgentProfileOut.description:
What a person with `ai.use` learns of an agent to talk to: no instructions, no
connection. `kind`: `external` for one that works from outside (plan M8): it
answers no message here.
AgentProfileOut.title: AgentProfileOut

AgentRunOut.description:
What a message to an agent started: its run (`id`; possibly one already waiting,
which answers this message too), or no run and why (`reason`: `ai.unavailable`,
`agent.draft`, `agent.paused`, `agent.responsible_inactive`,
`agent.connection_unavailable`, `run.thread_reply`, `run.waiting`). `agent_id`:
the agent it asked (the DM's, or the one a mention named).
AgentRunOut.title: AgentRunOut

AgentSkillOut.description:
`available`: whether the agent may use it now (active, and organisation-wide or
of a space the agent reads); a run also needs the person and the place to read it.
AgentSkillOut.title: AgentSkillOut

AgentSkillsOut.description: `version`: the agent's (setting the skills changes it).
AgentSkillsOut.title: AgentSkillsOut

AgentSpaceOut.description: A space the agent is a member of, with its `role` there.
AgentSpaceOut.title: AgentSpaceOut

AgentToolOut.description:
One tool for this agent: its own `level` (the lowest that allows it) and
`effect`; `default` (from the agent's level; an external tool's is `block`: it
needs an entry), `entry` (the agent's, or null) and `effective` (what a run gets).
`external`: set for an external MCP server's tool (name `ext_…`; a write tool is
level 4 and at most `confirm`), null for the catalog's. `via_mcp`: only for an
external agent (plan M8): the catalog tool can reach its token over `/mcp` (offered
there, level 2 at most); false for every other agent and tool.
AgentToolOut.title: AgentToolOut

AgentToolsOut.description:
An agent's tool grants: every tool of the catalog (a fixed, short list, so not
paged), then the organisation's usable external tools and those with an entry
(approved ones only, at most `mcp_servers/tools.MAX_APPROVED_TOOLS` of them, plus at
most 100 entries: a hard cap instead of pages, as the list is one versioned
document the PUT replaces whole). `version`: the agent's.
`max_level`: the highest level the caller may give the agent (above 2: admins
only).
AgentToolsOut.title: AgentToolsOut

AgentToolsPut.description:
All of the agent's entries (those left out are removed); each can only tighten
what the level allows. With the agent's `version`.
AgentToolsPut.title: AgentToolsPut

AgentUpdate.description:
Fields left out stay as they are; `connection_id` and `model` go together. A
personal agent takes its owner's connection and model anew with every change. The
kind stays; an external agent takes no connection or model and no level above 2
(422 `agent.external_invalid`).
AgentUpdate.title: AgentUpdate

AgentWritePolicy.description: How agents write pages in a space (plan M6 decision 8).
AgentWritePolicy.title: AgentWritePolicy

AiLockIn.description: Lock a page or a file for AI, or lift the lock; `version` as read (stale → 409).
AiLockIn.title: AiLockIn

AiPolicy.description: A space's AI policy (spec 7.3), stored on `space` (`modules/ai/policy.py`).
AiPolicy.title: AiPolicy

ApprovalDecide.description:
`approve` or `reject`; `reason` goes to the model (as untrusted text) on a
rejection; `version`: the approval's, as read.
ApprovalDecide.title: ApprovalDecide

ApprovalExternalOut.description:
The external MCP server and tool an approval's call goes to (plan M8 decision
8); their names are in `summary` ("<server> · <tool>").
ApprovalExternalOut.title: ApprovalExternalOut

ApprovalOut.description:
A tool call waiting for (or given) a person's release. `summary`: the tool and
what the system resolved of the call's arguments (a ticket's key, a status's name,
the ids of what it changes; never a text the model chose), or for an external
tool its server and tool; only for the person asked (null for others, module
review M8 5, L1). `args`: the call's arguments, only for the person asked
(null for others). `diff_url`: for a page's new content, where that person reads
the diff against the page as it is now (`GET`), instead of the text. `step` and
`call_id`: the call it waits for, as the run's journal names it (the step a run
link points at). `outcome`: what became of the call once released: `ran`, or
`stale` (what it would change had changed, so nothing ran); null before.
`reason`: the person's reason for a rejection, and `args`, only for the person
asked; for everyone else both are null and `redacted` is true (as in the run
view, review M6 finding 6). `external`: for a call of an external tool (it sends
`args` to that server once released), else null. `personal`: asked because the
run carries the asker's personal mark (every release then but a message into its
DM alone with her): what is released is written (or sent) where others can read
it now or later (module review M8 2; M8 5, L2). `reads`: the call only reads (a
catalog tool that writes nothing); under the mark its card says so instead of
that others can read what is released.
ApprovalOut.title: ApprovalOut

AssigneeIn.description:
A person, or (plan M6 decision 7) an agent: assigning an agent needs `ai.use`
and `ticket.assign`, and starts its work on the ticket.
AssigneeIn.title: AssigneeIn

AssignmentsOut.description:
The standard assignment and whether people with `ai.use` may create personal
agents; `version` guards both and the group list.
AssignmentsOut.title: AssignmentsOut

AttachmentOut.title: AttachmentOut

AuditOut.description: `actor_name`: the acting person's display name (None for other principals).
AuditOut.title: AuditOut

AuthorizeOut.description: Where the browser goes to approve the connection.
AuthorizeOut.title: AuthorizeOut

AutomationOut.description:
`abilities`: what the caller may do with it now. `upcoming`: its next terms from
now (none for an event rule, or once done). `redacted`: the caller sees it but
may not read its place, so `instruction`, `place.name` and `place.ticket_number`
are null (`words.py`). `term_errors`: terms in a row the due loop could not fire
and set aside (0: none).
AutomationOut.title: AutomationOut

AutomationUpdate.description:
Only its owner; the kind stays (422 `automation.kind_immutable`); a new schedule
computes the next term anew.
AutomationUpdate.title: AutomationUpdate

BaseUrlSpec.description: The instance's address, which the admin may change (a self-managed GitLab).
BaseUrlSpec.title: BaseUrlSpec

BoardCellOut.description:
A person's tickets in one status: how many, how many changed status since the
board's `changed_since`, the first of them in board order, and the cursor for more
(`GET /api/spaces/{space_id}/board/{status_id}?assignee=<id>|none`).
BoardCellOut.title: BoardCellOut

BoardColumnOut.description:
A status of the board: how many tickets it holds under the filters, the first
of them in board order (priority, due date with none last, number), and the
cursor for more (`GET /api/spaces/{space_id}/board/{status_id}`).
BoardColumnOut.title: BoardColumnOut

BoardOut.description:
The space's statuses in their order, each a column. Grouped by assignee
(`group_by=assignee`, the daily view): `columns` carry the statuses and their
counts only (no tickets), `rows` the people (by name, at most 100,
`rows_truncated` beyond; the row of the unassigned last) and `changed_since` the
moment the last working day began (0:00 UTC; on a Monday: Friday's).
BoardOut.title: BoardOut

BoardRowOut.description:
A person's row (`assignee` null: the tickets assigned to nobody), a cell per
status of the space in order.
BoardRowOut.title: BoardRowOut

BudgetIn.description:
At least one limit (422 `ai.budget_limit_missing`); `version`: the one read, or
null to create (409 `ai.budget_version_conflict` if the subject has one meanwhile).
BudgetIn.title: BudgetIn

CardOut.description:
A run's card (plan M6 task 7): what it waits for, `approval` or `question`, by
id (`GET /api/approvals/{id}`, `GET /api/questions/{id}`, for those who may see
it). The message's `body_md` is the card's summary or the question.
CardOut.title: CardOut

ChannelUpdate.description: Fields left out stay as they are; null clears the topic. A name cannot be null.
ChannelUpdate.title: ChannelUpdate

CheckIn.description: `model`: which model (route) to try; left out, the connection's standard model.
CheckIn.title: CheckIn

CheckOut.description: The outcome as a state, never with the provider's own words.
CheckOut.title: CheckOut

ChildCounts.description: How many children the ticket has, per status category.
ChildCounts.title: ChildCounts

ClientUpdate.description:
Only the fields sent change; `client_secret` replaces the stored one, `null`
removes it (a public client).
ClientUpdate.title: ClientUpdate

ConnectionCreate.description:
Left out: `base_url` is OpenAI's; `models` is `gpt-6-luna` for `openai`, else
empty; `param_family` is `max_completion_tokens` for `openai`, else `max_tokens`;
`data_location` is `local` for `local`, else `external`. The first model is the
connection's standard model.
ConnectionCreate.title: ConnectionCreate

ConnectionOut.description:
`streaming`: whether calls to it may stream (never for `b_api`). `prices`: per
model, where set (usage costs stay empty without).
ConnectionOut.title: ConnectionOut

ConnectionUpdate.description:
Fields left out stay as they are; `secret: null` removes the secret. The kind
never changes (sending it is 422).
ConnectionUpdate.title: ConnectionUpdate

ConnectorUpdate.description:
Only the fields sent change; `secret` replaces the stored one. An `oauth`
connector stays one (its tokens change by connecting and disconnecting), and no
other connector becomes one.
ConnectorUpdate.title: ConnectorUpdate

ConversationOut.description:
`can_post`: whether the caller may write here now (the right in the space, and
the channel not archived). `created_by` is null for what the system set up.
`version` guards writes (send it back; stale → 409). A direct message lists its
`participants` and, on its own (`GET /conversations/{id}`), every admin
`inspections` of it; both are empty for other kinds. `page_id`: a page thread's
page (null for other kinds). `fresh_start_at`: where the person started her DM
alone with an agent afresh (its agent sees nothing from before; null: never).
ConversationOut.title: ConversationOut

DailyCardOut.description:
A ticket of the daily view; `changed`: its status changed (or it was made) since
the board's `changed_since`.
DailyCardOut.title: DailyCardOut

DefaultIn.description: `target: null`: no standard, so only people and groups with an assignment have AI.
DefaultIn.title: DefaultIn

DiffOut.description:
Line by line from `from_number` to `to_number`; a changed line is a `delete`
followed by an `insert`.
DiffOut.title: DiffOut

DirectoryEntryOut.description:
Who can be added to a space or written to. Deliberately no email or role: any
member may read it. `kind`: an agent's kind (`external`: it works from outside
through `/mcp` and answers nothing here by itself, plan M8); null for people and
groups.
DirectoryEntryOut.title: DirectoryEntryOut

DiscoveryOut.description:
A proposal for an OAuth client, found from an MCP server's address; the
endpoints are None unless `status` is `ok` (`modules/oauth/discovery.py`).
DiscoveryOut.title: DiscoveryOut

DmOpen.description:
The other people (the caller is added); 2 to 9 people in all. Or, with
`agent_id` and no `user_ids`, the caller's conversation with that agent.
DmOpen.title: DmOpen

DmOut.description:
A direct message in the caller's list: `last_message_at` is its newest
top-level message (null before the first).
DmOut.title: DmOut

Effect.description: What a tool does: reads, proposes (a human decides), or writes.
Effect.title: Effect

EpicOut.description: An epic with how many children it has per status category (its progress).
EpicOut.title: EpicOut

EventType.description: What an event rule listens to (decision 8).
EventType.title: EventType

FiringOut.description:
One term of the log: how it went, the run it started, whether a heartbeat's
run answered `HEARTBEAT_OK` (nothing delivered).
FiringOut.title: FiringOut

Grant.description: How an agent may use a tool (spec 8.1), from loose to strict.
Grant.title: Grant

GroupMemberIn.description: People only in M1; agents join in M6.
GroupMemberIn.title: GroupMemberIn

GroupsIn.description: The whole ordered list; for a person in several groups the first one wins.
GroupsIn.title: GroupsIn

HitConversation.title: HitConversation

ImportResultOut.description: `created`: pages, folders without a file of their own included.
ImportResultOut.title: ImportResultOut

InspectableDmOut.description: What an inspecting admin learns before an inspection: who, and when, no content.
InspectableDmOut.title: InspectableDmOut

InspectionNoteOut.description: An admin looked into this direct message (spec 5.5): when, and who.
InspectionNoteOut.title: InspectionNoteOut

InspectionOut.description: Read the DM's messages at `/admin/dm-inspect/{id}/messages` until `expires_at`.
InspectionOut.title: InspectionOut

InstallIn.description:
A server (and what it needs) from a catalogue entry. The admin brings only the
access and its scope; every tool is still approved one by one.

- `none`: no credential.
- `shared`: one shared connector, created here: `bearer`/`header` with `secret`,
  `oauth` with an OAuth client (`client_id`, `client_secret` if confidential),
  connected afterwards (`POST /api/ai/connectors/{id}/authorize`).
- `personal`: each person connects their own; `oauth` creates the OAuth client
  they connect with, `bearer`/`header` need nothing more here.
InstallIn.title: InstallIn

LastRunOut.description: The latest term: how it went (`outcome`), its run and how that ended.
LastRunOut.title: LastRunOut

LinkStartOut.description: Where the browser goes to link an account (the provider's sign-in page).
LinkStartOut.title: LinkStartOut

LinkedPageOut.description: A page the ticket links (one the caller sees).
LinkedPageOut.title: LinkedPageOut

McpSettingsOut.description:
`enabled`: whether every active person but guests holds `mcp.use`.
`data_location`: what an MCP client counts as for the spaces' AI policy.
McpSettingsOut.title: McpSettingsOut

MeOut.description:
`permissions`: the system-wide actions the caller holds; clients decide what to
show from these (and from a space's `my_role`), never from the role's name.
`ai_model`: with `ai.use`, the name of the model the caller's AI assignment gives
them (nothing else about the connection); null without.
MeOut.title: MeOut

MessageAuthorOut.description: Who wrote a message, with the name to show (null if unknown).
MessageAuthorOut.title: MessageAuthorOut

MessageCreate.description:
`parent_id`: a top-level message of the same conversation, to reply in its
thread. `client_id`: the client's key for this message; sending again with the
same key returns the first message (200) instead of a second one. `mentions`:
whom the text mentions (`@[Name](user:<id>)`); at most 50.

mentions.description: the people the message mentions (user ids)
mentions.title: Mentions

MessageCreate.title: MessageCreate

MessageHitOut.description:
A message (`id`); `parent_id`: the thread it is a reply in (null: top level).
`snippet` and `score` as for pages.
MessageHitOut.title: MessageHitOut

MessageOut.description:
`author` is null for system messages; those carry `system` instead (null for
all others) and an empty `body_md`: their stored body holds ids the reader may not
be allowed to see, `system` only what is named for the reader (review M4 P1). A
deleted message keeps its place with `deleted_at` set and an empty `body_md`.
`reply_count` and `last_reply_at` belong to top-level messages (their thread).
`run_id`: an agent's message names the run that wrote it (AI mark: `kind=agent`).
`via_token`: a person's message written through an access token at `/mcp`, the
token's name (AI mark of an external AI client, plan M8).
`mentions`: the people mentioned who may see the conversation; `reactions`: by
emoji, the first reacted with first. `card`: set for a run's card (`kind`
`approval` or `question`). `personal`: an agent's message that holds what the
person read through her own connector (module review M8 2); only where she is
alone with the agent.
MessageOut.title: MessageOut

MessageUpdate.description: `mentions` left out: the message keeps whom it mentions; given: replaces it.

anyOf.description: the people the message mentions (user ids)

MessageUpdate.title: MessageUpdate

MessageWriteOut.description:
`not_notified`: the mentioned ids that were not stored: people who may not see
the conversation, and ids of nobody (indistinguishable on purpose; an agent a
mention asked is not among them). `agent_run`: for a new message in a DM with an
agent, or one that mentions an agent the writer may ask, the run it started or why
none (null otherwise, and for a resend).
MessageWriteOut.title: MessageWriteOut

MoveCategory.description:
Into the first status of `category` in the ticket's space (422
`ticket.category_empty` without one); `version` is the ticket version read.
MoveCategory.title: MoveCategory

MyBoardOut.description:
My tickets of every space I may read, by category: open, active, review, done
(done: finished in the last 14 days; cancelled ones are not shown).
MyBoardOut.title: MyBoardOut

MyCardOut.description: A ticket on my board, with the name of its space.
MyCardOut.title: MyCardOut

MyColumnOut.description:
A status category: how many of my tickets it holds, the first of them in board
order (priority, due date with none last, number), and the cursor for more
(`GET /api/tickets/my-board/{category}`).
MyColumnOut.title: MyColumnOut

MyUsageOut.description: The caller's own usage in the period (whole UTC days).
MyUsageOut.title: MyUsageOut

OidcSecretIn.description:
Either the secret itself (`value`, stored encrypted; needs `HERD_SECRET_KEY`) or
the name of an environment variable `HERD_OIDC_*` (`env`).
OidcSecretIn.title: OidcSecretIn

PageHitOut.description:
A page. `snippet` is plain text: render it as text and highlight what stands
between `⟦` and `⟧`. `score` orders the hits (higher is better); it has no unit.
PageHitOut.title: PageHitOut

PageMove.description:
`parent_id` null: the top level. `position` among the new siblings, 0 first;
left out: at the end, or where the page is if its parent stays.
PageMove.title: PageMove

PageOut.description:
`version` guards writes (send it back; stale → 409). `collab_generation` changes
whenever open live-editing sessions of the page end. `tags`: tag ids, by name.
`no_ai`: locked for AI (spec 11). `reviewed_at`: the last review (publishing or
"mark as reviewed"; null for a draft); `review_due`: the space's review interval
has passed since (plan M7 decision 11).
PageOut.title: PageOut

PageUpdate.description: Fields left out stay as they are; neither may be null.
PageUpdate.title: PageUpdate

ParticipantOut.description:
A person in a direct message (one who was deactivated stays listed), or its
agent (`type` `agent`, listed after the people).
ParticipantOut.title: ParticipantOut

PasswordChangeIn.description: A person's own new password; the current one proves it is them.
PasswordChangeIn.title: PasswordChangeIn

PendingCountOut.description: How many self-registered accounts wait for approval.
PendingCountOut.title: PendingCountOut

PersonNameOut.description: Who caused a timeline entry: a person, or (plan M6) an agent (`type`).
PersonNameOut.title: PersonNameOut

PersonOut.description: `name` is null only for someone the organisation does not know (any more).
PersonOut.title: PersonOut

PersonalAgentsIn.description:
Allow (or stop) personal agents for everyone with `ai.use`; off, existing
personal agents stop working (`agent.personal_disabled`).
PersonalAgentsIn.title: PersonalAgentsIn

PersonalServerOut.description:
A server that acts with each person's own connector, and whether the caller
has connected theirs.
PersonalServerOut.title: PersonalServerOut

Price-Input.description: A model's price per million tokens (EUR); cached tokens count as input.
Price-Input.title: Price

Price-Output.description: A model's price per million tokens (EUR); cached tokens count as input.
Price-Output.title: Price

ProposalAcceptIn.description:
`version`: the proposal's. `merged_content` with `page_version` (the page's
version it was merged against): the text to write instead of the proposal, after
a 409 `proposal.base_outdated`.
ProposalAcceptIn.title: ProposalAcceptIn

ProposalAuthorOut.description: A person or an agent, by name (null if it is gone).
ProposalAuthorOut.title: ProposalAuthorOut

ProposalDetailOut.description:
With the proposed `content_md` and `diff`, line by line from the base (empty for
a new page) to it; null when the texts are beyond `HERD_DIFF_MAX_LINES`
(`too_large`). For an open change: `page_version`, the page's version now (name it
with `merged_content` when accepting); and when the page's content is no longer
the base, `current_content_md` and `merge` (null when too large).
ProposalDetailOut.title: ProposalDetailOut

ProposalMergeOut.description:
The three-way merge of base, proposal and the page now: `merged_content` when it
merges cleanly (null with conflicts), and the merge in `segments`.
ProposalMergeOut.title: ProposalMergeOut

ProposalOut.description:
A proposal without its content. `kind`: `change` of `page_id`, based on its
version `base_version`; or `new`, a page `title` under `parent_id` (null: the top
level), whose `page_id` is the page it became once accepted. `ai`: made by an agent
(`run_id`: its run) or by a person's AI client through an access token
(`via_token`: the token's name, plan M8). `decided_by`/`decided_at`: who
accepted, rejected or (its author's person) withdrew it, and when;
`decision_reason`: a rejection's reason; `result_version`: the page version an
acceptance wrote (null if the page held that content already). `version`: name
it when deciding (stale → 409).
ProposalOut.title: ProposalOut

ProposalSegmentOut.description:
`clean`: merged `lines`; `conflict`: the stretch as in the base, as proposed and
as on the page now (the other three lists are empty for the other kind).
ProposalSegmentOut.title: ProposalSegmentOut

ProviderCheckOut.description: `code` is None when discovery and the JWKS answered as OIDC promises.
ProviderCheckOut.title: ProviderCheckOut

ProviderCreate.description:
`google`: issuer and scopes are the preset's (`issuer`, `scopes`, `trust_email`
are refused); `generic`: `issuer` is required, `scopes` must hold `openid`.
ProviderCreate.title: ProviderCreate

ProviderUpdate.description: Only the fields sent change; `client_secret` replaces the stored one.
ProviderUpdate.title: ProviderUpdate

QuestionOut.description:
An agent's question; `question` and `answer` only for the person asked (for
everyone else null, with `redacted` true: the model's words, as in the run view).
QuestionOut.title: QuestionOut

ReactionOut.description: People who reacted with `emoji`; `mine`: the caller among them.
ReactionOut.title: ReactionOut

ReadPositionOut.description:
The caller's read position: the message she read up to and when it was written;
both null before she read anything there.
ReadPositionOut.title: ReadPositionOut

RefreshOut.description:
How reading the tool list went: counts of tools new, with another fingerprint
and no longer listed; all 0 unless `status` is `ok`.
RefreshOut.title: RefreshOut

RunEventOut.description:
One step of a run (model call: usage and the answer's parts; tool call: name,
arguments, result, the spaces it came from; stop: the reason). `redacted`: parts
the reader may not read are left out (`agents/runs.py`); the asking person always
gets everything. `tokens_*`, `cost` (model calls with a price) and `duration_ms`
(model and tool calls) where the step recorded them, null otherwise.
RunEventOut.title: RunEventOut

RunOut.description:
A run as the run view shows it. `asker_*`: the person who asked (whose rights it
read with, who is billed); `steps`: its model calls; `attempt`: its take-ups by a
worker, `recoveries` those after a lost worker; `wait_until`: while `waiting`,
when it ends unanswered; `stop_reason` once `done`; `cancel_requested`: someone
